purpose: Literature-backed starting data for pyJMAK phase transformation and AF microstructure modeling.

phase_stability.baseline_assumption: 4140 is treated as a transformable low-alloy steel. During hot forging it is expected to be austenitic above the austenitization range; during cooling/quench, pyJMAK may predict ferrite, pearlite, bainite, and martensite depending on the supplied thermal history.

austenitization_temperature_c.notes: Use as a process-level prior for interpreting whether AF thermal histories should be modeled as fully austenitic before cooling.

martensite_start_temperature_c.notes: Screening prior from the pyJMAK steel example. Replace with measured or alloy-specific CCT/TTT data when available.

notes: The pyJMAK input file included with this codebase uses generic steel transformation tables as a prior.
For thesis-level predictions, replace the generic TTT/JMAK coefficients with 4140-specific CCT/TTT data or fit them against dilatometry/hardness/microstructure.

critical_strain_model.implemented_approximation: The code stores Q and the critical-strain prefactor/exponent directly in the same Zener-Hollomon-style interface used for 316L. This preserves the trend but should be calibrated for exact Lin et al. normalization.

austenite_grain_growth_prior.notes: Use this form for future explicit grain-growth implementation. Current mixed REX code uses simplified SRX recrystallized-grain priors and should be calibrated to measured AF final grain size.

implemented_mixed_model_defaults.status: transparent defaults for screening; calibrate before quantitative claims

drx.family: Lin et al.-style 4140 hot-compression DRX prior mapped into the common Zener-Hollomon Avrami interface

srx.family: Sellars-style SRX screening prior for low-alloy steel
srx.notes: Placeholder prior until 4140 AF interpass microstructure data are available.

mdrx.notes: Placeholder prior until 4140 AF interpass microstructure data are available.
